capabilities.contract: An instruction to staff is classified as plain communication — never delegation — whenever Carson's responsibility ends once the message is delivered (the recipient only needs to receive information, come/wait/meet somewhere, or respond personally, with no outcome to verify afterward). It is classified as delegation whenever the recipient owes a verifiable outcome Carson must keep tracking and follow up on. This is a semantic axis, not a syntactic one: it does NOT depend on imperative mood, a '[command] + person + "to" + verb' construction, whether the owner is named as the target, any fixed verb list, or any specific phrase — a vocative/direct-address instruction ('Christopher, come to the kitchen now.') is classified identically to an equivalent 'Tell/Ask/Have/Get' construction, and an owner-target phrase ('call me') is classified on the same axis as a third-party-target one ('come to the kitchen'). Classification: no task is created, no confirmation link is sent, and acknowledgement wording is communication-style, never task-style. Typed and voice Carson behave identically because both route through the same classifier and the same sendDelegation()/createAndSendDirectMessage() convergence points.

capabilities.contract: A fresh hosting/guest-arrival instruction uses the captured owner transcript as its authoritative source and supersedes older hosting state. Once a hosting operation is awaiting clarification, contextual and action-like replies such as 'Plan it for 8 PM' belong to that same operation and retain its operation id, occasion, date, location, and authority; only an explicit introduction of a different hosting event may supersede it. Hosting completeness is independent of proposal/execution authority: occasion, date, time, location, guest count, and an explicit dietary-restriction state must be resolved; explicit 'at home' is a valid location and no guest count may be defaulted or inherited. `executeProposedPlan` independently re-derives completeness immediately before any idempotency claim, task/message persistence, Waiting/follow-up state, or external delivery and fails closed with the canonical clarification when anything is missing. A known person is not automatically an eligible assignee: autonomous hosting selection may use only an explicitly non-family person with an operational staff role or staff relationship, and the execution boundary must resolve the exact person id/name within the authenticated owner account and re-check that eligibility before any task/message persistence or external delivery; notes, communication history, phone reachability, and WhatsApp consent never confer staff eligibility. An ineligible assignment fails the whole plan closed without substitution or partial send, while explicit owner-named direct communication remains a separate permitted path. Exactly one complete plan executes exactly once; delivery results are truthful; late callbacks, reconnects, and session shutdown cannot restore or execute an older operation.

A real production incident (PRs #68/#69, documented in RA7ETBAL_STATE.md's 'Hosting plan integrity guards' entry) had Carson orally claim a two-recipient hosting proposal was sent when `execute_instruction` was never called to persist it, then falsely tell the owner both recipients received instructions — the exact 'silently fail while Carson claims success' failure class this entire hardening project exists to catch, on this capability specifically. `RA7ETBAL_STATE.md`'s own 'Type to Carson is advisory-only' product decision (2026-07-25) already groups 'hosting plans' with reminders/delegations/staff messages/calendar events as voice-only, state-changing execution; its 'protected systems' list separately names hosting alongside delegations and owner decisions. 216+ pre-existing tests in ops-intelligence.test.ts already cover idempotency, truthful per-recipient delivery, and worker-role correctness — this capability has been protected in engineering practice all along, just never formalized in this registry or the required CI gate.

capabilities.contract: For covered consequential owner turns, the validated tool result is the single owner truth. Canonical execution evidence and canonical owner presentation are distinct: durable operation/task/message/delivery records retain the complete instruction and evidence, while displayed, stored, and spoken owner text contains only the concise verified outcome and next state. It must identify actual successful recipients, preserve every partial/failure fact and owner-attention requirement, and must not expose staff-message bodies, raw hosting summaries, payloads, IDs, or internal structures. Covered hosting client-tool responses carry a machine-marked speech contract whose owner_result must be spoken verbatim without additions or changes. ElevenLabs remains conversational on ordinary turns but cannot add/remove recipients, hide failures, invent persistence/delivery, change clarification/proposal/execution state, or contradict a covered canonical result. Hosting uses the captured owner transcript for intent/authority, binds results to the current turn and durable operation where available, and rejects late prior-operation results; transcript inference and session shutdown have no hosting execution authority.

capabilities.contract: Google Calendar OAuth initiation requires a valid authenticated Ra7etBal session; the server derives the user identity exclusively from the verified Supabase JWT and never from client-supplied input. OAuth state is a cryptographically random, single-use, 10-minute-lived token whose SHA-256 hash (never the raw value) is stored server-side bound to the verified user_id in the dedicated google_oauth_states table. The callback validates state atomically (a single DELETE ... RETURNING against google_oauth_states) before accepting any OAuth result -- missing, malformed, unknown, expired, and already-consumed state all collapse into the same zero-rows-returned rejection, and none of them ever triggers a Google authorization-code exchange or a profiles write. A valid callback obtains user_id only from the consumed state record, never from the state value itself. Existing authenticated Calendar read/create/update/delete/history routes (api/google-calendar.js routes 3-7) are outside this contract and must remain behaviorally unchanged.
capabilities.business_importance: critical — Tier 1. Registered 2026-08-16 (Carson Engineering Hardening Project, Remediation 3) after fixing a real, confirmed OAuth-CSRF account-linking vulnerability: initiation previously accepted an unauthenticated, client-supplied ?userId= and passed it straight through as the OAuth `state`; the callback trusted that value verbatim to decide which profiles row received the Google refresh token. Anyone who knew (or obtained through any other channel) a victim's Supabase user id could complete Google's consent with their own Google account and silently redirect that victim's Ra7etBal Calendar integration to the attacker's own Google Calendar, with zero interaction from the victim and no Ra7etBal authentication of their own. `api/google-calendar.js` was previously excluded from Impact-Aware CI entirely (see the removed carson-impact-exclusions.json entry) on the stated basis that it was 'not yet a registered Tier 1 capability' and 'contains no logic touching any of the 14 registered capabilities' contracts' -- that justification did not hold once this file's real security logic was examined directly, the same pattern already corrected once for api/anthropic.js in Remediation 2.

api/google-calendar.js (Google's own OAuth redirect back to this same handler with ?code=...&state=...)
files_functions: api/google-calendar.js:handler (Route 1 -- authenticated OAuth initiation; Route 2 -- OAuth callback / state consumption)
capabilities.rollback_risk: medium — a defect could either (a) reject all legitimate Calendar connections (availability regression, safely visible as a 500/error redirect, no data-integrity risk) or (b) reopen the identity-binding gap this remediation closes (security regression). No existing user data is migrated or altered by the new table; rollback (DROP TABLE) only removes in-flight, already-expired-within-10-minutes OAuth attempts, never a completed connection (those live in profiles, untouched by this migration).
capabilities.verification_status: PRODUCTION VERIFICATION PENDING (application/business-logic layer AND database layer both independently proven; production deployment is the only remaining step) — application logic covered by 17 unit tests (12 in api/google-calendar.oauth-state.test.js: unauthenticated/malformed-token rejection, identity derived exclusively from the verified JWT with a spoofed client userId proven ignored, high-entropy state generation, hash-not-raw-value storage, per-user state uniqueness, 10-minute expiry, missing/unknown/expired-state rejection with zero Google token exchange and zero profile write, successful consumption binding to the correct user, single-use consumption modeled at the code-path level, and a no-secrets-in-logs assertion; 5 in SettingsModal.google-calendar-oauth.test.ts proving the client no longer sends a raw userId and only navigates after a successful authenticated pre-flight). Database layer independently proven against a genuine, ephemeral real-PostgreSQL instance (google_oauth_states_verification.sql, wired into the required carson-tier1-db-contracts.yml check, reusing its existing bootstrap/postgres-service infrastructure -- no parallel test system built): migration applies cleanly; state_hash uniqueness enforced (real unique_violation caught); user_id foreign key enforced (real foreign_key_violation caught); ON DELETE CASCADE genuinely removes the dependent row; anon and authenticated genuinely cannot select/insert/update/delete (real insufficient_privilege caught for all eight cases, not a grants-table check); service_role can create and consume; an expired row is rejected by the exact application query with zero rows returned and the row left untouched; a valid state is consumed exactly once (sequential replay returns nothing); and -- the specific gap this verification closes -- two genuinely concurrent consumption attempts for the same state cannot both succeed, proven with a real second PostgreSQL connection via dblink (the same pattern already established by owner_notifications_concurrency_verification.sql): session A holds an uncommitted DELETE's row lock, session B's identical concurrent DELETE is proven to actually block on it (not silently race), and after A commits, B's resumed statement returns zero rows. All of this was also independently exercised locally against a real Postgres 16 instance (forward migration -> verify -> rollback -> confirm table removed -> reapply -> reverify, all passing) before being wired into CI. Concurrent-request atomicity is therefore no longer an assumption stated from Postgres's documented locking semantics -- it is directly, repeatably demonstrated. The database migration has NOT yet been applied to production and the PR has not yet merged; this capability cannot be marked PRODUCTION VERIFIED until both happen and a live post-deploy check confirms the vulnerability is closed.
unresolved: The database migration (supabase/migrations/20260816_google_oauth_states.sql) has not yet been applied to production Supabase -- it requires explicit approval before being run, per this project's standing database-safety rule. capabilities.contract: Carson's spoken opening line (opening_line dynamic variable, spoken verbatim by the ElevenLabs dashboard's configured first message) is a Chief-of-Staff briefing, not a database/app-state summary. It must apply relevance judgment before information reaches speech: only critical/action-needed items (urgent decisions, overdue commitments, escalations, failures), today/tonight-relevant items, and genuine accomplishments are spoken — routine background state (e.g. a recurring automation merely sent-but-unconfirmed) is deliberately silent. A truthful Waiting statement may identify the responsible person and confirmation status, but must not recite the stored staff instruction or message body; detailed instructions remain available in durable execution evidence and Communication History. On the first session of a kind (morning/night) each day, the full brief is given; on every later session that same day, an unchanged actionable item is never repeated, but a genuinely new or materially changed one (new/newly-firing reminder, newly escalated/failed automation, new Needs You owner-decision, materially changed calendar event) always surfaces. Morning Brief and Night Sweep track their own first-session and already-surfaced-material state completely separately, so an earlier Morning Brief session can never suppress the day's first legitimate Night Sweep, and vice versa. Task-label categorization (e.g. distinguishing a food/grocery task from an unrelated chore) is canonical and shared — Morning Brief and Night Sweep must never independently drift on the same description.
capabilities.business_importance: high — this is the deterministic mechanism behind Carson's entire proactive-briefing promise (PR #24 reminder inclusion plus every other Morning Brief/Night Sweep actionable signal). A defect here either silently drops real, actionable information from the owner's very first interaction with Carson each session (PR #24's original failure mode), or floods it with low-value noise that erodes trust in the briefing (the "8 automation loops"/"food task" incidents) — both are product-contract failures, not just technical bugs.

Updated 2026-08-18 (four passes): pass 1 fixed automation double-counting (dedupeLatestPerAutomation) and "automation loops" wording plus the disconnected post-midnight greeting. Pass 2 implemented the Chief-of-Staff relevance contract: routine (non-escalated/failed) automation status is never spoken in either brief, Needs You is wired in as a 4th domain distinct from Waiting On Others, owner_notifications was investigated and deliberately excluded, Night Sweep's duplicated label-categorization logic is deleted in favor of morning-brief.ts's canonical taskLabel(), and completions use natural outcome language. Pass 3 replaced Waiting On Others's age-based (escalated-OR-stale-beyond-72h) gate with isMaterialWaitingItem()'s three consequence-based signals (escalated_at, isQualityOwnerReviewStatus, overdue/due-today). Pass 4 closes a live-acceptance-discovered automation-task relevance leak using the existing automation_runs.task_id provenance. Updated 2026-08-19 after PR #315 owner acceptance exposed a separate presentation leak: an actionable Waiting item identified Christopher correctly but appended the complete stored hosting instruction to the fresh-session opening. Morning and Night material items now report the person/status only and leave detailed instructions in durable records.

isMaterialWaitingItem()'s three signals (escalated, quality-review-owner-decision, overdue/due-today) are the smallest safe set the current data model reliably supports — not independently product-validated against a broader sample of real usage patterns, and there is no existing signal for "blocks another commitment" or a delegation-specific deadline distinct from due_at, so that class of relevance genuinely cannot be detected today without inventing semantics the data doesn't contain. May need revisiting after live acceptance if a real gap surfaces.

DATA-LIFECYCLE FOLLOW-UP (explicitly out of scope for this fix, per product decision): automation-generated tasks accumulate indefinitely — each firing creates a brand-new tasks row (via automation_runs.task_id) instead of updating/superseding the prior one, and none are ever archived or marked done automatically. Production evidence (read-only, 2026-08-18): 7 separate never-archived 'Update the Rahet Bal master plan.' task rows spanning Aug 12-18, 6 each for 'Charge your phone' and 'check on Claude skill files'. This remediation makes the ROUTINE ones correctly silent in the briefing regardless of this accumulation, but the underlying persistence/lifecycle question (why isn't the prior occurrence's task row closed when a new one is created?) is a separate architectural issue, not addressed here.
